newsitem.title: USA: PG&E power marketer wins part of supply bid.
newsitem.headline: PG&E power marketer wins part of supply bid.

text.p: PG&E Energy Services, the unregulated power marketing arm of PG&E Corp, said Wednesday it will supply up to 100 megawatts (MW) of firm power to members of the Association of Bay Area Governments (ABAG), beginning next January.

The one-year contract represents about one sixth of the total amount of capacity awarded by ABAG to several suppliers as a result of a competitive bid process that began last autumn, PG&E said in a statement.
ABAG is a joint powers agency of nine counties and 95 cities throughout the San Francisco Bay Area.

PG&E Energy Services' contract with ABAG is one of several electricity supply agreements it has entered into in recent months, including contracts to provide power to the City of Ashland, Oregon and to a Nestle USA facility in Othello, Wash.

ABAG members are currently supplied by Pacific Gas and Electric Co, PG&E's regulated monopoly utility, but are allowed under California's deregulation proceedings to buy power from other suppliers as of next January.
